extracted.intended_audience: general readers, librarians, children's_literature authors and scholars
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize the standards and procedural features governing the selection of the annual Newbery Medal winner (the most distinguished American children’s book of the previous year), including eligibility, who judges, and how runners-up are treated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary criterion — 'most distinguished American children’s book of the previous year'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Newbery Medal is an annual award given to the author of the most distinguished American children’s book of the previous year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This wording defines the quality standard ('most distinguished') and the temporal eligibility (the previous year). The phrase is the central evaluative standard used to choose the winner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationality / origin eligibility — 'American' book
rubrics_metrics.description: The award is given to the author of an American children’s book (i.e., the Newbery Medal recognizes American children’s books).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award’s scope is limited to American works/authors; entries are therefore judged on that national/jurisdictional basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal eligibility — 'of the previous year'
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible books are those published in the previous year (the award recognizes the most distinguished book of the prior year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This imposes a publication-year window for consideration; books outside that year are not eligible for that year’s medal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended recipient — author (not illustrator)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Newbery Medal is presented to the author of the book; illustration-recognition is handled by the separate Caldecott Medal for artists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies that text/literary distinction (authorial achievement) is being judged by the Newbery, while illustration excellence is assessed by the Caldecott.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection body / committee composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The judging committee responsible for selecting the award’s winner comprises educators, librarians, book reviewers, publishers, and children’s literature experts, all of whom are members of the Association for Library Service to Children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee’s multidisciplinary composition indicates the kinds of expertise considered in evaluation (pedagogy, librarianship, criticism, publishing, scholarship). Being members of the Association for Library Service to Children is a procedural requirement for judges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of runners-up — Newbery Honor Books
rubrics_metrics.description: Judging committees also cite notable runners-up of the prize, and in 1971 such titles were designated Newbery Honor Books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond naming a single winner, the committee may designate additional titles as Honors; this is an established practice and a formal category of recognition since 1971.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation context — awarded at the ALA annual conference
rubrics_metrics.description: The medal is presented at the annual conference of the American Library Association, alongside the Caldecott Medal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the procedural/publication context in which winners are announced and celebrated; it is part of the award’s formal practice.
